reason: Chrome always sends `Connection: keep-alive` on HTTP/1.1; hyper's H1 client does not emit it and H2 forbids it. Only HTTP/1.1 origins can observe this.
Chrome sends the RFC 9218 Priority header only on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3. turbo-surf builds request headers before ALPN chooses the protocol, so HTTP/1.1 requests carry it too.

Chrome derives each stream's HEADERS-frame priority (weight 256/220/183/147 and a dependency chain) from the request priority. The wreq transport applies one connection-level stream priority (exclusive, dependency 0, weight 256) to every request; the connection preamble (SETTINGS, WINDOW_UPDATE, pseudo-header order) matches.

Chrome interleaves page-set (author) headers such as x-battery inside its own order. Author header names are unknowable ahead of time, so wreq appends them after the measured browser order; every browser-owned header keeps Chrome's order.

Sec-CH-DPR needs the document's devicePixelRatio when the request is built; ClientHints has no render geometry, so the hint is not offered (the same holds for Sec-CH-Viewport-Width, classed as environment).
Critical-CH restarts are not implemented (request_context.rs module docs); the first request is compared and matches.
Native live layout does not load @font-face resources (it reports them unsupported), so no font request is made.
Chrome's browser UI requests /favicon.ico for every committed document. A browserless engine has no tab strip; emitting the request would need a real UI-driven reason.
Native form submission into another browsing context (target=<iframe name>) throws `Native form submission to another browsing context is not supported`.
navigator.userAgentData is a plain object rather than a NavigatorUAData instance, so toJSON() and the prototype getters are missing. Values (brands, mobile, platform, every high-entropy hint) match.

Chrome 156 ships V8 15.6.75.19; turbo-surf's stock engine is V8 15.0.245.2 (native155 SDK: 15.5). Engine builtins (Iterator.zip, Iterator.prototype.includes/join), error messages and ICU data follow the embedded V8 and are never spoofed. Closed by the harness/detection/engine re-version step.
CSS.supports answers from turbo-dom's real parser, which does not accept these Chrome 156 properties/functions yet. Faking `true` would contradict the computed style the same page can read.

Window own-property names native exposes and Chrome 156 does not: three absent-interface stub names from runtime.rs's stub list (PaintWorkletGlobalScope is worklet-only, webkitAudioContext was removed, StorageAccessHandle is not a Window global) and one internal global (`__name`, the esbuild keepNames passthrough in runtime.rs; the hydration fetch drain counter `__pendingFetches` is private since turbo-surf#83). Pinned by name so any new extra global is a tell. Interface owners: API-INVENTORY.json / issue #28.
